topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and frames the complexity and importance of the complement system.

topics.label: Foundations of complement and central C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles, naming conventions, and core C3 activation mechanism of the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three biochemical pathways that recognize pathogens and converge to reach the threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream immune responses driven by activated complement to destroy pathogens and stimulate inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct clinical presentations and disease susceptibilities associated with deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the molecular strategies pathogens employ to avoid complement-mediated destruction, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and introduces the topic of the next session.
